observation.what_happens: A red ball hanging from a black string swings side to side below a support. It is released from the right side and keeps swinging as a pendulum through the clip with no catch or stop visible.

thread length = 0.6 m (“धागे की लंबाई साठ सेंटीमीटर है।”)
reasoning: Theta oscillates about 0 with amplitude ~0.14 rad and period ~1.58 s on a constant-radius circle, matching a simple pendulum with L~0.62 m. Amplitude falls ~15% over 6.4 s, indicating weak damping in air. Candidates compete undamped linear textbook vs exact sine with linear viscous damping vs exact sine with quadratic aerodynamic drag.

law.title: Large-angle pendulum with quadratic air drag
law.summary: A pendulum slowed mainly by air resistance pushing harder when it moves faster.

fitted.title: Large-angle pendulum with quadratic air drag
fitted.summary: A pendulum slowed mainly by air resistance pushing harder when it moves faster.

candidates.ifItWins: Energy loss is dominated by turbulent air drag that grows as speed squared, not pivot viscosity.

candidates.ifItWins: The swing loses energy in proportion to speed from pivot friction and slow air viscosity, giving exponential amplitude decay.

Quadratic drag here is effective and can mix air resistance with pivot friction.

headline: Pendulum swings wide with slight air drag slowing it.
finding: It swings side to side as a wide pendulum with gravity pulling at g = 9.81 ± 0.2 m/s² on a string of length L = 0.6 m and air drag slowing it with strength q = 0.108 ± 7.94e-4 1/rad. It keeps matching the later swings closely.
